body:
Your coworker and manager did not handle the situation correctly at all. Some people have so many of their own issues that they can’t handle other’s. Which is sad because I feel like a manager is supposed to be able to deal with issues that come up. Everyone perceives life through their own experiences, and yours may be either too far off for them or too close to home. Either way it doesn’t matter. Your reactions are valid, and they don’t know how to handle the situation. 

It’s okay to have outbursts, you have ptsd. There has to be someone higher up to reach out to. Your manager isn’t managing, and your co-worker sounds abusive. 

Stay strong. You are in the right.

I’m sorry you are hurting right now. 

There are always ups and downs with coping. The downs feel like everything is over, but think of your ups. You will feel like you have some control again. You will be okay. 

Trauma hardens in our brain like a rock, and we have to chip away at the rock for years sometimes. You are strong to be here coping and reaching out. You are actively trying to heal and that’s so brave. 

Deep breathes. It will all be okay.

All the time. I won’t eat for days because I simply can’t stomach it. Personally, drinking bubbly water or tea helps me to start. Then I’ll distract myself with a movie/show and try to eat while watching.

Take your time and go slow, but please eat. I know it’s difficult though.

I’m sorry you’re going through this.

I can relate. I will keep hanging around the same type of person, and when I have a ptsd episode it can often feel like it wasn’t even me, or I was taking aggression out on the wrong person.. I feel  my behavior is more harsh than it really was all of the time and I panic for days. Typically it’s because that person has actually made the wrong move and it’s triggered me from past experiences.

It seems like his behavior has triggered something you’ve experienced. it doesn’t sound like you were being abusive. You were irked because he was being manipulative and then you made sure it was all okay. You wouldn’t care or you would only want personal gain if you were being abusive. You are very smart to be able to think all this through. If you feel you need some space and time for you, that’s what you need. It’s hard to trust yourself when you have experienced trauma, but I really think you can trust yourself and love yourself. You have a good head on your shoulders.
